headline: Abu Dhabi has created a company called TAMM Global to sell its AI-powered government services platform to other countries.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: an official announcement of a new state-backed export company, but the performance figures are the government's own.
importance_line: Residents of countries that buy the system, and their governments, could get ready-made digital services, and it shows a Gulf state selling AI-run public services as an export, but the performance figures are Abu Dhabi's own and the report names no customer governments.
summary: The National reports that Abu Dhabi's Department of Government Enablement, acting on a directive from Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, the emirate's crown prince, has set up TAMM Global, an independent company that will license the design and methods of TAMM, Abu Dhabi's single digital gateway to more than 1,200 public and private services, to governments abroad. The department says satisfaction with the platform rose to 94.5% from 78% in 2022, before AI was added, and that the cost of providing services fell 30%, figures that come from Abu Dhabi itself.
notes: Arabian Business (pool source, HTTP 403) not opened; the story was read at The National, which reports the official announcement of the Department of Government Enablement. The National says TAMM launched in 2005, which looks odd for the current platform, so the entry leaves that date out.
